target_customer: Employers in Brazil who offer salary advance as a benefit; employees are the end users
problem: Brazilian workers face expensive payday loans for emergencies; Facio advances part of next salary through employer payroll.
business_model: B2B2C fee per advance, employer payroll linked

technical_complexity.rationale: Payroll integration and credit and compliance work in Brazil; standard fintech engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Employer payroll integrations and a planned financial institution license create friction for rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition seen; no dated incumbent move sourced.

market_need_then: Facio said Brazilian payday loans were more expensive; Brazil Journal says the idea came from US salary advance products such as Dave.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional fintech press coverage, no brand assets found.

outcome_analysis: Facio started in 2019 as financial education plus salary advance and raised a $5M seed in November 2020 led by Monashees and ONEVC. It remains active with about 36 staff, and databases report a later Series A in 2024 that was not verified. It appears to have survived on employer distribution, but evidence on revenue is conflicting.
notes: Unverified: pre-seed $1.5M Feb 2020 (BounceWatch only); Series A about $11M Aug 2024 (CB Insights and FundedIQ aggregators); Getlatka calls it bootstrapped with $5.4M revenue, which conflicts. Crunchbase News says total about $6.9M including a 2019 angel round. Competitor lists are aggregator based and undated, so left empty. Name origin not found.
